input.quote: 14.1 Assignment. Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights or obligations hereunder, whether by operation of law or otherwise, without the prior written consent of the other party. Notwithstanding the foregoing, either party shall have the right to assign this Agreement in connection with the merger or acquisition of such party or the sale of all or substantially all of its assets related to this Agreement without such consent, except in the case where such transaction involves a direct competitor of the other party where consent of the other party will be required.
input.rationale: Section 14.1 is the only assignment provision, and no clause anywhere gives Commerce One a termination or re-pricing right on Corio's change of control (§ 11 termination triggers are breach and insolvency only), so we are outside walk-away territory. The clause already delivers two fallback elements mutually: successor assignment in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all related assets without consent, and a consent requirement for all other assignments. It fails the fallback on two material terms: the consent requirement carries no reasonableness standard (so Commerce One could refuse an affiliate or other assignment arbitrarily), and the successor carve-out has no written-notice mechanic. We therefore propose the two shortest conforming edits to bring § 14.1 to the fallback level, leaving the mutual direct-competitor consent proviso and the null-and-void sentence untouched. We have not sought the preferred affiliate carve-out, since a no-consent affiliate exception is inconsistent with the fallback requirement that all non-successor assignments need consent.

proposal.summary: Add reasonableness standard to assignment consent and written notice for successor assignments in § 14.1.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We accept the mutual assignment construct but need two fixes: consent to any other assignment must not be unreasonably withheld, and the merger/asset-sale carve-out should run on prior written notice to the other party. This is our fallback assignment position.
